current_evidence: Not verified: the WebFetch budget was used up before any TMBC page could be read. Web search shows file 3989 is the checklist on the council's 'Local validation requirements for planning applications' downloads page, but the search index still lists it under the older slug '...from-15-september-2025-'. The council also has a 'draft local validation list may 2026' (file 4778) and a 'review local validation checklist planning applications' consultation page, so the 1 August 2026 version is probably the adopted successor, but this was not confirmed from document text.

issues.detail: The site plan requirement is placed under exactly the three application types the source exempts from it: Variation of condition s73, Discharge of conditions and Non-material amendment. It is also mislabelled 'Block plan / Site plan', but the quoted rule is about the Site Location Plan.
issues.evidence: Grokbot's own excerpt: 'Site Location Plan: All applications, except Non-Material Amendment, Approval of Details Reserved by Condition and S73 Applications where the original site area is used.'

issues.detail: About 20 requirements are all marked 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', while Householder, Outline, Reserved matters and Listed building consent show '(none)'. Grokbot's own excerpts show some items cover householder works. Site sections apply to 'alterations to garden levels such as raised patios'. A roof plan applies to 'alterations to an existing one'. The FRA exemption only covers minor domestic extensions with no new bedroom space. The tab text also says a DAS accompanies 'applications for listed building consent'. Examples of INFERRED rows: Air Quality, Arboricultural, Archaeology, Ecology, Lighting, Viability.
issues.evidence: Householder row: 'No specific local requirements identified for this application type'. Section drawings: 'Required where the proposal involves a change in ground levels ... alterations to garden levels such as raised patios'.

issues.detail: List date 2026-08-01 was taken from the URL slug ('Date basis: url'), not from text in the document. The same file id 3989 is indexed with the slug 'from-15-september-2025' and in one result with the title 'Draft Local validation requirements checklist'. A separate May 2026 draft also exists. The adoption or effective date needs confirming from the document itself.
issues.grok_comment: The basis is indeed the URL, but the document itself is headed "Draft Local validation requirements checklist ... 3 August 2026", so the August 2026 date is supported by the text; the real issue is that it is a draft.
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. The August 2026 date is in the text. The real issue is that this is a draft list, so its adoption status should be recorded.

issues.detail: The Parking provision row's trigger runs into the Planning Obligations section, so parking appears to be triggered by 'Major developments' and S106 text. The Planning Obligations row starts mid-sentence with the end of the parking text.
issues.evidence: '...parking stress in the surrounding highways. (CPZ) Planning Obligations – Draft Head(s) of Terms Application Trigger: Major developments Policy Driver: Policy CP25...'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are fragments or content descriptions, not statements of when the item is required. Floor plans/Elevations: 'to the floor plan of the property.' Housing mix: 'dwelling types (housing mix).' Ventilation: 'conditioning or extraction equipment is required.' Heritage Statement: 'It may also be necessary to produce a Heritage Statement (see above).', which is taken from the archaeology section. Affordable Housing: a content list with no threshold. Archaeology: '18 An archaeological assessment should include...'. Arboricultural: content only. Transport Assessment: 'may propose mitigation measures'. Fire Statement: form wording with no height or storey trigger.
issues.evidence: Grokbot app_type_rows trigger_excerpt values as quoted

issues.detail: One tab item runs together three separate requirements: elevation annotation (building height AOD), drawing scale, and the start of the Design and Access Statement section. This gives a garbled requirement under 'Drawing / document standards'.
issues.evidence: 'Annotate overall proposed building height (AOD) of the application site and both neighbouring properties Scaled at 1:50 or 1:100 Design and Access Statement A Design and Access Statement required in a pdf format...'

issues.detail: Several 'Submission rules' items are fragments, headings or policy-driver text rather than requirements: 'All drawings and documents must be submitted in PDF format. (expect where outlined below) Document Structure:'; 'Transport Statements) may be submitted as a multi-page PDF.', which is cut off at the start; 'All Plans and drawings should be in pdf format and include: 2', which ends in a page number; and 'Achieving Well Designed and Beautiful Places. (paragraph 135) Core Strategy Policy CP1 and CP24 Required in a pdf format.', which is a policy reference.

The 'CIL Additional Information / Form' row is based only on a reference to the CIL Regulations 2010, probably the Reg 122 tests in the S106 section. Tonbridge and Malling has not adopted a CIL charging schedule, so a CIL form requirement is likely spurious. This should be confirmed against the source.
issues.evidence: trigger_excerpt: 'with the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended).'

issues.detail: The Transport Assessment requirement is filed in the tab under 'Submission rules' rather than as a requirement.
issues.evidence: 'Required in a pdf format a Transport Assessment (TA) should be submitted as part of any planning application where the proposed development has significant transport implications.'

issues.detail: Several triggers contain page numbers, typos or leftover text from neighbouring sections: FRA 'application. 21 Flood Risk Assessment Application Tigger:'; LVIA 'person. 24 Landscape and Visual Impact Assessment'; Retail 'acceptable 28 Retail Impact Assessment'; Air quality starts '2022 TMBC air quality report – Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council'.

summary: The live source could not be fetched or compared because the shared WebFetch budget was used up. Grokbot's link (file 3989, '1 August 2026' slug) is probably the council's current checklist, but its date comes from the URL only. Grokbot's own data shows clear errors: the site location plan is put under the three exempt application types, Householder is wrongly shown as having no local requirements, and many triggers are garbled or not requirements at all.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
